lines.japanese: 「なんだよもう、俺もラーメン食いたかったのに」
lines.english: “Come on. I wanted ramen too.”

lines.japanese: 俺は言われるがままミニバンの助手席に乗りこんでドアを閉めた。狭い車内に白い息が消える。
lines.english: I did as I was told, climbed into the minivan's passenger seat, and shut the door. My white breath vanished into the cramped cabin.

lines.japanese: パルクレープ閉店後しばらく冬の路上に置きさられていた密閉空間は、震える歯が噛みあわないほどの冷気で満たされていた。俺は寒さに体を揺らしながらシートベルトを締めた。
lines.english: The minivan had stood shut on the winter street since Paru Crêpes closed, filling with cold so fierce my chattering teeth could hardly meet. Shaking, I fastened my seat belt.

lines.japanese: 「途中でコンビニでも寄ってやるよ」
lines.english: “We'll stop at a convenience store on the way.”

lines.japanese: 運転席のパルさんがエンジンキーを回した。ダッシュボードの吹き出し口から、乾いた唸りと冷たい突風がほとばしる。俺はエアコンのルーバーを限界まで下へ向けて風を封じた。
lines.english: Paru turned the ignition key. A dry groan and a blast of cold wind burst from the dashboard. I forced the vent louvers as far down as they would go, damming the air.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　コンビニ？」
lines.english: “Huh? A convenience store?”

lines.japanese: 「カップラーメンでも買って、向こう着いてから好きなだけ食いなさいよ」
lines.english: “Buy some cup ramen. Once we get there, you can eat as much as you like.”

lines.japanese: そうじゃない。空腹を満たしたいというより、今夜はメンマやプラチナと朝まで騒いでいたかった。そんな気分だったんだ。
lines.english: That wasn't it. Filling my stomach mattered less than spending the rest of the night raising hell with Menma and Platinum. That was the mood I was in.

lines.japanese: なのにパルさんは俺を、ラーメン屋の温かな湯気香るカウンターから引きはがしてここまで連れてきた。
lines.english: But Paru had torn me away from the ramen stand's warm, fragrant steam and dragged me out here.

lines.japanese: 「つか、どこ行くのかいいかげん教えろよ」
lines.english: “Anyway, are you ever gonna tell me where we're going?”

lines.japanese: 「そうねえ、ある意味うちらにとっちゃ観光地だよ。ひひ、お楽しみお楽しみ」
lines.english: “Well, in a sense, you could call it a tourist attraction for people like us. Heehee. You'll see, you'll see.”

lines.japanese: やつはハンドルの上に頬杖をつき、助手席へ顔を向けてにやついていた。暖気が済むまでにはまだ少しかかりそうだった。
lines.english: She propped her cheek on one hand over the steering wheel and smirked toward the passenger seat. The engine apparently needed a little longer to warm up.

lines.japanese: よく分かんないけど、パルさんが楽しみって言うならそうなんだろう。俺はヘッドレストに頭を預けて軽く目を閉じた。
lines.english: I didn't really get it, but if Paru said it would be fun, it probably would. I rested my head against the headrest and lightly closed my eyes.

lines.japanese: 冬の冷たさに体じゅうの痛みが疼いていたが、同時に緊張の糸が切れたあとの気だるさもあった。体が疲れている。まぶたの裏にあったかいシャワーと布団が浮かびあがった。
lines.english: The winter cold set every ache in my body throbbing, but beneath it lay the lassitude that comes when the last thread of tension snaps. My body was tired. Behind my eyelids appeared a hot shower and a warm bed.

lines.japanese: 耳には時代遅れのハイパーテクノが流れこんでくる。パルさんがカーオーディオを点けたみたいだ。
lines.english: Outdated hyper techno poured into my ears. Paru must have turned on the stereo.

lines.japanese: 「そういやさあ」
lines.english: “Hey, you know...”

lines.japanese: 目を閉じたまま、しかし眠気がやってこないよう声を出すことにした。
lines.english: I kept my eyes shut, but made myself talk to hold sleep at bay.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん、さっきメンマの店で言ってたじゃん。マルチネスもすぐ退院できそうだって」
lines.english: “Paru, back at Menma's you said Martinez oughta be out of the hospital soon, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、電話口じゃピンピンしてたよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. He sounded fit as a fiddle on the phone.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあアレだな、メンマの分と合わせて退院祝いしねーと」
lines.english: “Then we gotta throw a party when they both get out—him and Menma.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、メンマ入院してないし──ほんっとに、あいつどんな体してんだかねえ」
lines.english: “Menma was never admitted. Seriously, what is that man made of?”

lines.japanese: 呆れ混じりの優しい嘲笑に、俺も釣られて鼻を吹いた。エンジンより一足はやく車内が暖まったみたいだ。心地よいまどろみが忍びよってくる。
lines.english: Her gentle, exasperated laugh drew a snort from me. It felt as if the cabin had warmed a step ahead of the engine. Pleasant drowsiness crept over me.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なにあんた、眠いの？　なんだったら着くまで寝てなさいよ」
lines.english: “Hm? What, you sleepy? If you are, sleep till we get there.”

lines.japanese: 「や、大丈夫……ちょっと疲れてるだけだから……」
lines.english: “Nah, I'm good... Just a little tired...”

lines.japanese: なんとなく強がって、あくびを噛みころした。
lines.english: I made a pointless show of toughness and swallowed a yawn.

lines.japanese: 「そいやパルさんさあ……プラチナの自慢話、聞いたあ……？」
lines.english: “Oh yeah, Paru... You hear Platinum bragging...?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なんかドラマの仕事取れたらしいね。すでに五回ぐらい聞いたよ」
lines.english: “About landing a job on a TV drama? Yeah. I've heard it about five times already.”

lines.japanese: 俺は斜めに走るシートベルトの上で腕を組んで、鼻から長い息を吹きおとした。
lines.english: I folded my arms over the diagonal seat belt and let a long breath spill from my nose.

lines.japanese: 「俺も負けてらんねえなあ……そろそろ安定した仕事探すかなあ……」
lines.english: “Can't let him leave me behind... Maybe it's about time I found steady work...”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なんだい、気持ち悪いぐらい前向きじゃないか。もう寝惚けてんのか？」
lines.english: “Huh? Listen to you, so positive it's creepy. You asleep already?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ……」
lines.english: “Shut up...”

lines.japanese: 寝惚けてねえよ……ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ……。
lines.english: Not asleep... I'll fucking kill you, asshole...

lines.japanese: どこまで口の外に吐いたのか、もう分からない。
lines.english: I could no longer tell how much of that had made it out of my mouth.

lines.japanese: 俺はパルさんの楽しげな皮肉とシフトレバーを倒す音を子守唄代わりに、睡魔の誘惑を受けいれてひそかに落ちていった。
lines.english: With Paru's amused sarcasm and the clunk of the gearshift for a lullaby, I yielded to sleep's invitation and quietly sank.

lines.japanese: ナビゲーターシート越しのかすかな振動がいざなう浅い眠り。
lines.english: The faint vibration through the passenger seat invited me into a shallow sleep.

lines.japanese: 「なあ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 俺は最前列の長机のへりに、尻を預けて立っていた。そして片足の踵でとんとん床を叩きながら訊いた。
lines.english: I stood with my backside propped against the edge of the long desk in the front row. Tapping the floor with one heel, I asked him.

lines.japanese: 「あんた昔──その、俺らンこと知ったばっかのころ、言ったよな。心の病気だから医者に診てもらえって」
lines.english: “Way back—when you'd only just found out about us—you said it was a sickness of the mind, that we should see a doctor.”

lines.japanese: じいさんが顔を上げる。歴史の深い皺だらけの顔。病を背負い、教会内の「煩雑な人間関係に敗れた」というその顔は、優しい瞳そのままに、しかしもはや力強さを欠いて精彩を失っていた。
lines.english: The old man raised his deeply lined face. Illness had worn him down, as had the church’s tangled personal relationships, which he called a defeat. His eyes were still kind, but their old vigor had gone.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。やっぱそうするべきかな」
lines.english: “Hey. You still think that's what we should do?”
“Hmm.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは入れ歯の抜けたような老人の口を蠢かせた。
lines.english: The old man worked his lips like an ancient mouth missing its dentures.

lines.japanese: 「鷲介君から聞いていると思うが──」
lines.english: “I expect Shusuke has told you—”

lines.japanese: 錯覚だった。血の気の薄い薄い唇の奥に、少し黄ばんだ歯列が覗いていた。
lines.english: It had been an illusion. Behind those bloodless, paper-thin lips showed a row of faintly yellowed teeth.

lines.japanese: 「──少し前に、彼とふたりでお医者さまのところへ相談に行ったんだ。君たちのような症状をいくつも診てきたという、とても高名な先生だ」
lines.english: “—that some time ago, he and I went together to consult a doctor. A very eminent physician who has seen many cases with symptoms like yours.”

lines.japanese: 「彼はまず、現在の君たちがとても安定していることに驚いていた。それは個々の精神状態に関してもそうだし、任意によってある程度管理されている全体に関してもだ」
lines.english: “The first thing that surprised him was how remarkably stable you all are at present. He meant both the mental condition of each individual and the whole, which you are able to govern to some extent by mutual choice.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと」
lines.english: “What's that mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、つまりな……」
lines.english: “Ah. That is to say...”

lines.japanese: じいさんはのろのろと歩いてきて、通路を挟んだ俺の反対側の長椅子にゆっくり腰を下ろした。膝を折ったとき、唸るような息遣いがこぼれた。
lines.english: The old man shuffled over and slowly lowered himself onto the pew across the aisle. When he bent his knees, a groan escaped with his breath.

lines.japanese: 「ふう……つまりだ。こういった症例では、共生するそれぞれが深刻な人格障害を抱えている場合が多いと言うんだ。自閉的であったり反社会的であったり、破滅願望を持っていたり破壊衝動を持っていたり」
lines.english: “Whew... That is to say, in cases like yours, the coexisting personalities often carry grave personality disorders of their own. Some are withdrawn or antisocial; some harbor a wish for ruin or an impulse to destroy.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 破滅願望。破壊衝動。いまひとつピンと来ないが、物騒な響きの言葉だ。俺は他人事のように聞きながらぼんやり視線を下げた。
lines.english: A wish for ruin. An impulse to destroy. Neither quite landed with me, but the words had an ugly ring. Listening as though it concerned somebody else, I let my eyes drift downward.

lines.japanese: 長椅子の上で、皺だらけの枯れた手が膝の皿を叩いていた。じいさんの関節リュウマチはその頃もうすでに発病していて、右の膝がとくに痛いんだって、弱々しく笑いながら言ってた。
lines.english: On the pew, a withered, wrinkled hand patted his kneecap. The old man's rheumatoid arthritis had already set in by then. His right knee hurt worst, he had told me with a feeble smile.

lines.japanese: 「それから……大抵のケースにおいて、人格の交替は不規則に行われるらしくてね。五分で替わることもあれば、数日替わらないこともある」
lines.english: “And... in most such cases, it seems the changes between personalities occur irregularly. A switch may come after five minutes, or not for several days.”

lines.japanese: 「運転中、信号待ちでぼうっとしてるあいだに幼児の人格に替わってしまった例もあるし、台所で出刃包丁を持った瞬間、獰猛で攻撃的な人格に替わってしまった例もある」
lines.english: “There has been a case in which someone, idly waiting at a traffic light behind the wheel, changed into the personality of a small child. In another, merely taking up a kitchen cleaver brought out a ferocious, aggressive personality.”

lines.japanese: 「したがって多くの場合、ＤＩＤは当人や周囲に多大な影響を及ぼし、社会生活を送る上で困難や不都合をもたらすらしいのだが」
lines.english: “Thus, in many cases, DID has a profound effect on the person and those around them, creating difficulties and inconveniences in social life.”

lines.japanese: まるで老眼鏡でもかけ忘れたみたいに、じいさんは頭を引いてぎゅっと目をすぼめた。か細い喉仏。老いて灰色に濁った瞳が、一生懸命フォーカスを俺に絞っていた。
lines.english: As if he had forgotten his reading glasses, the old man drew back his head and narrowed his eyes. His Adam’s apple looked frail in his thin throat. Eyes clouded gray with age strained to bring me into focus.

lines.japanese: 「先生は君たちを、そういった先例と比較して『安定している』とおっしゃったんだ」
lines.english: “It was in comparison with such precedents that the doctor called you ‘stable.’”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺はすまして唇をとがらせた。なんだか誉められているような気になって、結論を急いだ。
lines.english: I pursed my lips in studied indifference. It almost sounded as if I were being praised, so I leapt ahead to the conclusion.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、病院行かなくてもいいんだ」
lines.english: “Then I don't gotta go to the hospital.”

lines.japanese: 「やはり行きたくはないか」
lines.english: “You truly don't want to go?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃまあ」
lines.english: “Well, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 強がっても仕方ない。正直に答えた。
lines.english: There was no point pretending otherwise. I answered honestly.

lines.japanese: 俺は≪病院≫が嫌いだ。嫌いというより、恐い。
lines.english: I hated hospitals. More than hatred, it was fear.

lines.japanese: 「だって……」
lines.english: “Because...”

lines.japanese: それは子供が注射器の針に竦みあがるのとは違う、もっと生存本能に訴える根源的な恐怖心だった。
lines.english: This was no child's terror of a hypodermic needle. It was more primal than that—a fear that spoke directly to the instinct for survival.

lines.japanese: 「だって病院に行ったら、俺とか鷲介みたいのは消されちゃうんだろ」
lines.english: “Because if I go to a hospital, people like me and Shusuke will get erased. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「消えるわけじゃない。みんなひとつになるんだ。君たちは鷹志君の中でずっと生きつづけるんだよ」
lines.english: “You will not disappear. You will all become one. You will go on living within Takashi.”

lines.japanese: 「……どうだか」
lines.english: “...Says who.”

lines.japanese: 顔をしかめて首をひねった。そんな言葉は気休めに思えた。
lines.english: I grimaced and tilted my head. It sounded like hollow consolation.

lines.japanese: 「その偉い医者はどうしろって？」
lines.english: “And what does this great doctor say we should do?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ……おそらく治療には気の遠くなるような時間と根気が必要になるそうだ。だから、当人たちに治療の意思がなくては改善も難しいという」
lines.english: “Hmm... He says treatment would probably demand a staggering amount of time and perseverance. Improvement would be difficult unless the patients themselves wished to be treated.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 俺は惨めな気持ちで鼻を鳴らした。治療だの改善だのの単語が引っかかった。それじゃあまるで俺の存在は悪質な腫瘍みたいじゃないか。
lines.english: I gave a miserable snort. The words treatment and improvement caught in me. They made my existence sound like a malignant tumor.

lines.japanese: 「それから先生はこう言われた──たしかに現状は安定している。しかし、いずれこの安定が乱される可能性は高い。だから治療は受けてほしい、本人のためにも、周囲のためにも」
lines.english: “He also said this: certainly, the present condition is stable. But there is a strong possibility that this stability will one day be disturbed. Therefore, he wishes you to undergo treatment—for your own sake and for that of those around you.”

lines.japanese: じいさんは背中を丸めて膝を撫でさすりながら、医者の言葉を俺に伝えた。リュウマチが辛そうだ。あのいつまでも若々しかった拳闘家が、ここ一年で十年分の老いに蝕まれてしまったみたいだ。
lines.english: Hunched over and rubbing his knee, the old man relayed the doctor’s words. The rheumatism looked painful. The boxer who had stayed young forever seemed to have aged ten years in the space of one.

lines.japanese: やつはよく、気が若ければ体も歳を取らないと言っていた。だからつまり──気が歳を取ってしまったんだろう。
lines.english: He used to say that if the spirit stayed young, the body would never age. So I suppose—that spirit of his had grown old.

lines.japanese: 俺は恨み言をぶつけるのが躊躇われるほど老いすぎた男に、窺うような目を向けた。
lines.english: I gave the man, now too old for me to hurl my grievances at, a searching look.

lines.japanese: 「あんたもその医者と同じ意見なの」
lines.english: “You agree with the doctor?”

lines.japanese: 「私か？　私は……」
次の言葉を探すじいさんの、張りのない頬が裏側から突かれてぽこっと尖った。愛敬のある癖だった。
lines.english: As the old man searched for his next words, his tongue poked one slack cheek into a little point. It was an endearing habit.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……私はやはり、障害を抱えている者ならば医師のもとでしかるべき治療を受けるべきだと思う」
lines.english: “Hmm... I still believe that anyone living with a disorder ought to receive proper treatment under a physician's care.”

lines.japanese: 俺は嘆息してあらぬ方へ首を曲げた。聞かなきゃ良かった。やつの真似をして舌先で頬の裏を突いた。視界の外でじいさんが言葉を続けていた。
lines.english: I sighed and turned my head away. I wished I hadn't asked. I copied him, prodding the inside of my cheek with my tongue. Beyond my field of vision, the old man went on.

lines.japanese: 「先生は君たちの症例をＤＩＤ──解離性同一性障害と呼んだ」
lines.english: “The doctor called your condition DID—dissociative identity disorder.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ、障害、障害……その異常性によって当人または社会が苦しむもの……ううむ……」
lines.english: “Hmm. Disorder, disorder... Something whose abnormality causes suffering to the person himself or to society... Hmmm...”

lines.japanese: 喉を鳴らすような音が聞こえて俺は向きなおった。じいさんが子供みたいに唇を突きだして、白髪の混じった後ろ頭をがしがしと掻いていた。
lines.english: I heard a sound deep in his throat and turned back. The old man had stuck out his lips like a child and was vigorously scratching the graying back of his head.

lines.japanese: 「どうなのかなあ……いまの君たちは、たしかにちょっとばかし特別な生き方ではあるが、立派に社会生活を営んでいるじゃないか。障害を来たしていない症状を障害と呼ぶのは、ちと矛盾してないかね」
lines.english: “I wonder... You may lead lives that are a little unusual, certainly, but you function perfectly well in society. Isn't it rather contradictory to call a condition a disorder when it causes no impairment?”

lines.japanese: じいさんは背筋を伸ばして腕を組んでいた。濁った瞳に色が戻ったようにさえ見えた。
lines.english: The old man had straightened his back and folded his arms. It almost seemed as if color had returned to his clouded eyes.

lines.japanese: しかし、それはその短いひとときだけだった。
lines.english: But only for that brief moment.

lines.japanese: 「ふう……とは言っても、しょせん私は素人だ。医者でも神の使徒でも何でもない。だから君たちは、私なんかより専門家の言葉を信じてほしい」
lines.english: “Whew... That said, I am only a layman. Neither a doctor nor an apostle of God. So I want you to trust a specialist's word over mine.”

lines.japanese: そう言ってまた背中を丸め、俯いて膝をさすり始めた。それはちょうど俺から目を背けているようにも見えた。
lines.english: With that he hunched over again, bowed his head, and resumed rubbing his knee. It looked almost as if he were turning his eyes from me.

lines.japanese: 「そっか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 俺はじいさんのそんな姿は見たくなかった。だから頷いた。
lines.english: I didn't want to see him that way. So I nodded.

lines.japanese: 「分かった。あんたがそう言うなら前向きに考えてみるよ」
lines.english: “All right. If you say so, I'll give it real thought.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ！」
lines.english: “Ah!”

lines.japanese: やつはほっとしたように破顔した。
lines.english: His face broke open in relief.

lines.japanese: 「だが自棄になることはない。先生のお考えとは違うかもしれんが、私はじっくり考えるぐらいの時間があってもいいんじゃないかと思うよ」
lines.english: “But there is no need to act out of desperation. This may differ from the doctor's opinion, but I think you can afford to take the time to consider it carefully.”

lines.japanese: 痰の絡んだようなしわがれ声で優しくそう言った。俺はちょっと面倒くさそうな顔を作って、じいさんのところまで歩いていった。
lines.english: He said it gently in a hoarse voice that rattled with phlegm. I arranged my face into mild annoyance and walked over to him.

lines.japanese: 「この辺かな」
lines.english: “Around here?”

lines.japanese: 床の上に屈みこんで、じいさんの膝に触れた。枯れ枝みたいな細さに驚いたが、表情には出さなかった。
lines.english: I crouched on the floor and touched his knee. Its dead-branch thinness startled me, but I kept it from my face.

lines.japanese: よく分からないけど、やつの手の動きを真似してマッサージした。やつはくすぐったそうに笑いながら俺の頭に手を置いた。眠たげな赤ん坊をあやすみたいに、その手が優しく揺れていた。
lines.english: I didn't really know how, but I copied the motion of his hands and massaged the knee. He laughed as if it tickled and rested a hand on my head. It moved gently, soothing a drowsy infant.

lines.japanese: 「あとさ」
lines.english: “One more thing.”

lines.japanese: 俺は五本の指の力加減を気遣いながら言った。
lines.english: I spoke while minding the pressure in each of my five fingers.

lines.japanese: 「羽田のおっちゃん達に負担とか迷惑かけたくないんだよ。だから……」
lines.english: “I don't wanna burden Uncle Haneda and the others. So...”

lines.japanese: 「タカシが卒業したら、俺と鷲介も働ける幅が広がると思うし、そしたら金の問題はなんとかなるかなって思うんだ」
lines.english: “Once Takashi graduates, there oughta be more jobs open to me and Shusuke. Then maybe we can work out the money problem.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……そうか、そうか……」
lines.english: “Yes... I see, I see...”

lines.japanese: ぽん、ぽん、と頭の上に優しい感触が降ってくる。しばらくその温かさに浸りながら、俺はもう一度繰りかえした。
lines.english: His hand patted my head gently, once, twice. I let myself bask in the warmth for a while before saying it again.

lines.japanese: 「約束する。タカシが卒業したら病院行ってみる」
lines.english: “I promise. Once Takashi graduates, I'll go to the hospital.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん……大丈夫だ、恐がるな……」
lines.english: “Yes, yes... It's all right. Don't be afraid...”

lines.japanese: 頭の上で広がった指が俺の髪を力強く撫でまわした。
lines.english: The fingers spread over my head and tousled my hair with sudden vigor.

lines.japanese: 「たとえ神様が見てなくても、俺は見ているからな」
lines.english: “Even if God isn't watching, I am.”

lines.japanese: そのときの温もりを俺はいまでも覚えている。
lines.english: I still remember the warmth of that moment.

lines.japanese: 「がんばれよ」
lines.english: “Keep going.”

lines.japanese: ──それはじいさんが教会を追いだされて遠い町へ行く、一週間前のことだった。
lines.english: —That was one week before the old man was driven from the church and went away to a distant town.
